name: Isis
label: Hydra Head
lede: Aaron Turner started Isis in Boston with his roommate Jeff Caxide while already running Hydra Head Records. Five albums later the band ended where it began, in Montreal, and came back once, in 2018, for a benefit.

eras.title: A revolving door in Boston
eras.text: Aaron Turner and Jeff Caxide started Isis in Boston as roommates, then went through members for two years before the five-piece that made every album settled. Early records came out on small labels, one of them Turner's own Hydra Head.

years.big: "It was just kind of me by default."
q: Both of us, having come from a hardcore background, gravitated towards the stuff that was more obtuse or abstract in nature.
years.src: Riot Fest: Autodiscography · Wikipedia: Isis (band) · Wikipedia: Hydra Head Records
years.h: Roommates Aaron Turner and Jeff Caxide start Isis in Boston
years.p: Drummer Aaron Harris and Chris Mereschuk, on electronics and vocals, fill out the first line-up. Turner is explaining how he ended up as the singer.
years.xp:
Turner says he was "really scared to play guitar and sing at the same time" and that nobody else would take the job. Wikipedia dates the band's formation to autumn 1997.

The records he and Caxide traded back then included Buzzoven, Neurosis, Today Is the Day and Earth. Turner was already running Hydra Head Records, which he started in 1993 as a distribution business while still in high school in New Mexico.

Getting to a stable line-up took two years. Turner's explanation: "a lot of bands didn't even last two years."

years.h: Montreal gets the first show
years.p: A demo cut at Salad Days Studios gets Isis onto stages in spring 1998. The tour that follows nearly ends the band.
years.xp:
Turner says personal friction nearly broke the band up after that first tour, until he and Caxide talked it through and decided to keep going.

The band picked Montreal again for its final show, on June 23, 2010.

years.h: Chris Mereschuk leaves after a summer tour with Cable's Randy Larsen
years.p: Larsen plays guitar on the East Coast run. Michael Gallagher and Jay Randall arrive the next year.

years.h: Mosquito Control is the first Isis record, on Escape Artist
years.p: The EP comes out on CD and LP. It plants the mosquito, an image that keeps coming back in the band's artwork and themes.

years.h: Michael Gallagher and Jay Randall arrive in time for The Red Sea
years.p: Gallagher comes from Cast Iron Hike. Randall, later of Agoraphobic Nosebleed, is the one who leaves.

years.h: Second Nature puts out The Red Sea
years.p: Gallagher's first record with Isis is Randall's last. It is pressed on CD, 8-inch vinyl and LP.

years.src: Wikipedia: Isis discography · Wikipedia: Hydra Head Records
years.h: Sawblade is the first Isis release on Turner's own label
years.p: The tour-edition EP starts as 200 handmade CD-Rs and 250 LPs on Hydra Head, the label Turner runs alongside the band.
years.xp: Hydra Head's first official record was a Vent 7-inch in 1995, after Turner moved to Boston for art school. He made the label a full-time job after graduating in 1999, the year of Sawblade.

years.h: Meyer from The Gersch takes Randall's spot, and the churn stops
years.p: [[Bryant Clifford Meyer|22c39a7c-d513-4091-8065-122bc8ebe68e]] joins on guitar and keyboards. Turner, Caxide, Harris, Gallagher and Meyer make every Isis album from here.
years.xp: The same five stay together until the end in 2010, and come back together once in 2018.

eras.title: Neurosis's label takes notice
eras.text: The first album came out on two labels and a split with Pig Destroyer followed. Then Neurot, the label tied to Neurosis, released a companion EP with a Godflesh remix.

yt: The Tower, live at Michigan Fest 2002
years.h: The debut, Celestial, comes out on Escape Artist and Hydra Head
years.p: Recorded in January and February 2000 at The Outpost in Stoughton, Massachusetts, with [[Matt Bayles|e294077f-71eb-401f-a36a-f2dbcbd75863]] engineering and mixing.
years.xp:
Turner has said the record deals with privacy wearing away as technology advances, handled in a "more primitive way" than on Panopticon four years later.

Decibel later ranked it 53rd among the decade's metal records and said it holds up "in ways different from their later work." AllMusic's William York went further and called it the band's best.

Ipecac reissued it in 2013, remastered by James Plotkin with new artwork by Turner.

years.h: Pig Destroyer and Isis share a Relapse 7-inch
years.p: Isis contributes a cover of a Godflesh song that first appeared on Sawblade.

years.src: Wikipedia: Celestial (Isis album) · Riot Fest: Autodiscography
years.h: Neurot releases SGNL›05, remixed by Godflesh's Justin Broadrick
years.p: The EP comes from the Celestial sessions, on the label tied to [[Neurosis|a9416fb3-4d28-4575-abae-f0d160be83ed]]. Broadrick remixes the title track.
years.xp:
Turner called SGNL›05 and Celestial "part of the same whole", and split them apart to avoid handing listeners a double-album debut.

Neurosis is one of the bands he names as a founding influence, along with Earth and Buzzoven.

eras.title: Water first, then surveillance
eras.text: Oceanic reached for water and ambient space, and Panopticon for surveillance, with a guest from Tool. Between them the band packed up for Los Angeles.

years.src: Wikipedia: Oceanic (Isis album) · Wikipedia: Isis (band) · Riot Fest: Autodiscography
years.h: Terrorizer names Oceanic the best album of 2002
years.p: Recorded in April and May 2002 at Fort Apache in Cambridge and New Alliance in Boston, produced with Matt Bayles. Maria Christopher of 27 sings on three songs.
years.xp:
It's a concept album: a man finds completion in a woman, then learns about her relationship with her brother, and drowns himself. Pitchfork gave it 9.1, Decibel ranked it fourth on its albums of the decade, and Rolling Stone placed it 72nd on its 2017 list of the 100 greatest metal albums.

Ipecac came through a friend, James Plotkin, and Mike Patton was already a fan. Turner said that by this record "I was starting to become more comfortable with singing and playing at the same time, actually enjoying it." The song Weight later turned up on Friday Night Lights.

years.h: Isis leaves Boston for Los Angeles
years.p: Turner moves Hydra Head's operations along with the band. Panopticon gets recorded there the next summer.

years.h: Panopticon borrows its name from Jeremy Bentham's prison
years.p: Recorded at Paramount Studios in Los Angeles in June and July 2004. Justin Chancellor of [[Tool|66fc5bf8-daa4-4241-b378-9bc9077939d2]] plays on the instrumental Altered Course.
years.xp:
Bentham designed the prison, and Michel Foucault wrote about it as a model of surveillance. The liner notes bring in Howard Rheingold and Alex Steffen. The cover is an aerial photograph of South San Bruno and South San Francisco; Turner said the link was "certainly intentional" but meant to be "subtle."

It entered Billboard's Top Independent Albums at No. 47, the band's first chart entry. Drowned in Sound's Mike Diver called it "the metal record of the year." Half the original analog master tapes went missing after the sessions.

years.h: A free show at the Los Angeles Museum of Contemporary Art
years.p: Isis plays for an exhibition of 1950s and 60s minimalist art, then takes Panopticon across North America, Australia, Japan and Europe.

years.h: Revolver lists Isis at number 12 among the heaviest bands
years.p: The list lands two months after Panopticon, the band's first entry on a Billboard chart.

eras.title: Opening for Tool
eras.text: Isis played its biggest rooms, made its most melodic album, and had mixed feelings about the attention. Turner has said he preferred smaller venues.

years.src: Wikipedia: Isis (band) · Wikipedia: Oceanic (Isis album) · Wikipedia: Isis discography
years.h: All of Oceanic, front to back, at KOKO in London
years.p: The show in Camden Town is part of All Tomorrow's Parties' Don't Look Back series. It is recorded and released as Live V.
years.xp: Live V came out in October 2009 on Viva Hate, on CD and double LP.

years.h: Isis opens for Tool and gets heckled at one show
years.p: The support slot on Tool's 10,000 Days tour puts the band in front of far bigger crowds than usual.
years.xp:
Turner said the band was "only heckled, that we noticed, at one show on that entire tour." An earlier bill was a different story: "We opened for Cradle of Filth, Emperor, and Usurper in Worcester, and the whole front row turned their back to us."

He also said he preferred smaller rooms, where he felt a better connection between player, music and listener. On the attention, Wikipedia prints him saying that fans taking a deeply personal interest in who he is "fucking freaks me out."

years.src: Wikipedia: In the Absence of Truth
years.h: In the Absence of Truth sings more and drones less
years.p: Recorded June 8 to July 2, 2006 and produced by the band and Matt Bayles. It reaches No. 6 on Billboard's Top Heatseekers.
years.xp:
At 64 minutes 49 seconds it's the band's longest. No lyrics were printed, but Turner confirmed the sources: Hassan-i-Sabbah, Don Quixote, House of Leaves and Labyrinths, with the record about "the power and nature of perception."

The band was split between New York and Los Angeles while making it, and Turner later said it suffered for that. Harris felt they pushed themselves too far. Metacritic scores it 70 out of 100; it peaked at No. 20 on Top Independent Albums. Decibel gave Tool its "Isis Rip-off Band of the Year" award.
play: Not in Rivers, but in Drops

eras.title: Said everything they wanted to say
eras.text: Wavering Radiant put Isis on the Billboard 200 for the first time, with a new producer. Then the five said they were done and played their last show in Montreal.

years.h: Joe Barresi takes over from Matt Bayles for Wavering Radiant
years.p: Aaron Harris says the work with Bayles had become "routine." Tool's Adam Jones plays on two songs.
years.xp:
Sessions ran from November 2008 to January 2009, with drums and keyboards tracked at Sound City in Van Nuys in about three and a half days. Barresi had worked with Tool, Queens of the Stone Age and the Melvins. Jones plays guitar on Hall of the Dead and keyboards on the title track.

Turner drew on Carl Jung's Memories, Dreams, Reflections, kept a dream journal, and quit smoking marijuana in 2008 to remember his dreams better. The record sold 5,800 copies in its first US week and peaked at No. 98, the band's first Billboard 200 entry. Metacritic gives it 79 out of 100.

The video for 20 Minutes / 40 Years, directed by Matthew Charles Santoro in November 2009, got airplay on MTV2.

years.h: Golden Gods name Isis best underground metal act
years.p: Revolver's awards hand the band its trophy a month before Wavering Radiant arrives on CD.

years.big: "We've done everything we wanted to do, said everything we wanted to say."
years.h: Isis announces it will break up after one last tour
years.p: The statement comes from the same five members who made every album. Bonnaroo and Australia's Soundwave are still on the schedule.
years.xp: The farewell dates had Baroness, Big Business, Cave In and the Melvins on the bills. Turner has said the band took up so much of his time that it kept him from other projects.

years.h: Isis finishes where it started, in Montreal
years.p: The final show is on June 23, 2010, five weeks after the break-up announcement.

years.h: Melvins and Isis share a Hydra Head split EP
years.p: Isis takes side B with Way Through Woven Branches and The Pliable Foe, both from the Wavering Radiant sessions.
years.xp:
Vinyl came a week before the July 13 CD. One Isis track had only been on the Japanese edition of Wavering Radiant; the other was new. The Melvins side holds alternate versions of Pig House and I'll Finish You Off.

Critics split: Decibel gave it 8 out of 10, and Pitchfork's Jess Harvell gave it 6.0, writing that Isis's climaxes "are so restrained you can almost miss them."

eras.title: After the tide
eras.text: Turner went on to Mamiffer, Sumac and more Old Man Gloom, and Caxide, Harris and Meyer to Palms with Chino Moreno. In 2018 all five came back for one benefit night.

years.h: Three ex-Isis members and Deftones' Chino Moreno start Palms
years.p: Jeff Caxide, Aaron Harris and Bryant Clifford Meyer team up with [[Chino Moreno|e61400d1-9434-4abc-ac7a-4f1dad60cfc7]]. The self-titled debut arrives on Ipecac on June 25, 2013.
years.xp:
Moreno, an Isis fan, said he was "excited to combine my sense of creativity with theirs." Caxide said Palms isn't Isis with a new singer, because "that's not exciting," and that he brought "ideas that I would never have presented to Isis."

Harris recorded and mixed the album.

years.h: Temporal collects demos, covers and remixes
years.p: Ipecac packs demos, remixes, covers and acoustic material into two CDs, or three LPs plus a DVD of videos.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hydra Head Records · Riot Fest: Autodiscography
years.h: Turner calls it the "imminent demise" of Hydra Head
years.p: He announces it on September 11, 2012. The label stops taking new releases in December but keeps running its back catalog.
years.xp:
The roster included Cave In, Converge, Kayo Dot, Boris, Jesu, Khanate and Botch. The Los Angeles office closed in May 2013, and the label made one exception, Oxbow's Thin Black Duke in 2017. In 2020 it pulled its catalog from Spotify, returned rights to artists and folded.

Turner's lesson from the label, which he took to his later SIGE Records: "I only want to work with people I know really well and aren't going to be shitheads."

years.h: Turner redraws the covers as Ipecac reissues three albums
years.p: Celestial returns on June 5, 2013, Panopticon on April 29, 2014 and Oceanic on November 4, 2014.

years.h: Isis becomes "Isis the Band" online
years.p: The name collides with the rise of the Islamic State in August 2014, so the band changes its social media name.
years.xp: Turner has said the confusion made things hard. He says he appreciates fans who still wear Isis gear, and calls it an act of courage.

years.src: Wikipedia: Aaron Turner · Wikipedia: Old Man Gloom
years.h: Sumac comes after Mamiffer and Old Man Gloom
years.p: [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] starts [[Sumac|9b98f3ed-d24a-479e-bd15-97c16de9f13f]] in 2014. Mamiffer is his project with his wife, Faith Coloccia; Old Man Gloom began in 1999 in Santa Fe.

years.src: Treble · Wikipedia: Old Man Gloom · Wikipedia: Isis (band)
yt: Celestial at the Wiltern, October 13, 2018, full set
years.h: Isis plays the Wiltern once more, billed as Celestial
years.p: All five take the stage for Cave In's Caleb Scofield's family, with Cave In, Pelican, Old Man Gloom and 27 on the bill.
years.xp: Scofield died on March 28, 2018 at 39 in a car accident in New Hampshire. The band wrote that he was "a dear friend, roommate and collaborator" as well as a touring partner. Every dollar raised went to his family, and the five played as Celestial, not Isis.
